sense: one book of a set or a long work

evidence: Nep. Att. 16.3: sēdecim volūmina epistulārum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: From volvō: a roll of writing, and so one book of a longer work. In poetry and post-Augustan prose also a coil or fold (of a snake, Verg. A. 2.208) or a wreath of smoke. Not the volume of sound (see volume, loudness).

terms.gloss: a book; one book of a work
terms.comment: The plain word for a book, and the usual way to number the parts of a work: liber tertius.

evidence: M. Aurel. ap. Fronto: in quīnque tomīs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Greek τόμος, a piece cut off; in Martial (1.67.3, Lewis & Short) a cheap roll of paper, in Marcus Aurelius one part of a longer work.

phrases.latin: sed quoniam duōbus superiōribus dē morte et dē dolōre dictum est, tertius diēs disputātiōnis hoc tertium volūmen efficiet.
phrases.english: but since death and pain were dealt with in the two earlier ones, the third day of the discussion will make this third volume.

sources: Lewis & Short: volumen · Lewis & Short: liber · Lewis & Short: tomus
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. volume (book).
